name: Lip stain

lead: A lip stain is a water-based colour that stains the lips rather than sitting on top, giving a sheer, matte, natural-looking flush. It evens and warms lip colour with little transfer.
It is a cosmetics category with a long history, from mid-century "kissproof" lipsticks to modern K-beauty lip tints.

paras: Applied to bare lips and built up to the desired intensity. Peel-off versions are peeled away after setting. Some people add balm for moisture.
Alcohol-containing formulas can be drying; any cosmetic dye may irritate or cause allergy in some people.

angle.text: A stain gives lips a natural-looking tint that wears longer than most lipsticks and resists transfer.

lead: A lip stain is a sheer, long-wearing lip colour that dyes the lips instead of coating them. It is usually matte, while a lip tint is similar but often glossier.[1]

Water-based stains soak into the skin, which reduces smudging and transfer; this made them popular with face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic.[1] They became popular in Korea in the 2010s, where they are typically less pigmented.[1]

paras: Water-based stains use soluble dyes, often with alcohol to dry quickly; alcohol can be drying. Cream versions use ingredients such as isododecane and dimethicone, and colourants may be synthetic or plant or mineral derived.[1]

Hazel Bishop is credited with an early kissproof stain lipstick. Benetint was created in San Francisco in 1976 by Jean and Jane Ford, later founders of Benefit Cosmetics. Peel-off stains became a social-media hit, with one topping TikTok Shop beauty sales in 2024.[1]

timeline.event: Benetint lip and cheek stain created in San Francisco.[1]
Lip tints become popular in Korea.[1]
